11.1b — Create PT: Build Day 1

Build day one, PT rules: write the LIST-CENTERED core. The list is the requirement graders poke hardest — today it goes in first, works alone, and prints so you can SEE the data move (input, behavior, output, remember).

Build Day ~50 min

The day's contract:

  1. The program RUNS — even if it only prints
  2. The list EXISTS and participates: add, remove, access, or traverse — not a decoration
  3. A Debug.Log rendering of the list's state after each change, so "behavior" is visible NOW (graders see a VIDEO later; you see the console today)

Starter-voice template for a list-centered core (adapt to your program — names matter for your WR answers):

private List<string> inventory = new List<string>();

public void AddItem(string itemName)      // procedure + parameter!
{
    if (!inventory.Contains(itemName))    // selection
    {
        inventory.Add(itemName);
        Debug.Log("added " + itemName + " → " + ListContents());
    }
}

private string ListContents()
{
    string s = "";
    foreach (string item in inventory)    // iteration
    {
        s += item + " | ";
    }
    return s;                             // output of a procedure
}

That one method pair already has: procedure, parameter, selection, iteration, list participation, observable output. Your 10.2c muscle, aimed at a rubric.

The WR2a pre-answer (5 min, write it NOW while coding): "The list ___ stores ___; the program appends when ___, removes when ___, and traverses to ___." Write the sentence the same day you write the code — future-you will not remember why the list exists; today-you does.

Close of Day ~5 min

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Run the program with the list visibly participating
  • Point at a procedure with a parameter and its CALL site
  • Show selection and iteration inside one algorithm
  • Read your WR2a sentence out loud and nod
